LESSON: READING 8.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION: VISUALS

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.2: Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals, part of Strand 8 in Grade 6 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why do we say a picture is worth a thousand words?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify information from visuals for information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. summarise information using a visual for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the role of summarising using visuals for effective communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify information from visuals for information,

   Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. summarise information using a visual for effective communication,

   Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate the role of summarising using visuals for effective communication.

   Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work jointly to study a visual related to the theme and discuss with peers,

2. make notes on information derived from the visuals and share with peers for review,

3. work jointly to summarise a text using a visual e.g. pictures, graphs, charts, mind maps,

4. display the visual on charts for peer review,

5. team up to prepare a mosaic piece using available materials on an idea related to the theme on technology.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work jointly to study a visual related to the theme and discuss with peers,
2. make notes on information derived from the visuals and share with peers for review,
3. work jointly to summarise a text using a visual e.g. pictures, graphs, charts, mind maps,
4. display the visual on charts for peer review,
5. team up to prepare a mosaic piece using available materials on an idea related to the theme on technology.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and Imagination: This is enhanced as the learner prepares a mosaic piece using available materials on an idea

related to the theme on technology.

● Self-efficacy: This is enhanced as the learner shows defining personal skills when summarising a text using visuals e.g.

pictures, graphs, charts, mind maps.

46

Values:
● Unity: This is promoted as the learner works harmoniously with peers to study a visual related to the theme.

● Responsibility: This is promoted as the learner exhibits accountability to accept input by displaying the visual on charts

in class for peer review.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

ICT: This is promoted as the learner interacts with information on technology for Digital Literacy.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept on visuals to their learning of creative pieces in Creative Arts.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify information from visuals for information,
2. summarise information using a visual for effective communication,
3. appreciate the role of summarising using visuals for effective communication.

Remember the key question: Why do we say a picture is worth a thousand words?
